sec: Hyperkalemia · ECG progression and acute treatment

items.q: Match each row of the hyperkalemia ECG table with its tracing description — 1) Around 4 mmol/L 2) 6 to 7 mmol/L 3) 8 to 9 mmol/L 4) Above 9 mmol/L … A) Normal complex with visible P wave B) Peaked T waves C) Atrial standstill with prolonged QRS duration and further peaking of T waves D) Sine wave pattern with absent P waves
items.exp: The ladder reads normal near 4, peaked T waves at 6 to 7, flattened P wave with prolonged PR and depressed ST at 7 to 8, atrial standstill with wide QRS at 8 to 9 and a sine wave above 9. (Book p975)

items.q: Between which potassium values does the table place flattened P waves, a prolonged PR interval and a depressed ST segment alongside peaked T waves?
items.exp: The third row of the table, 7 to 8 mmol/L, is the one that combines atrial changes with the peaked T waves. (Book p975)

items.q: Assess the first line of the acute regimen: I 10% calcium gluconate is labelled the drug of choice. II It is given because it shifts potassium into cells and lowers the serum level.
items.exp: Calcium gluconate is the DOC, but its stated mechanism is to raise the action-potential threshold to a less negative value without changing the resting membrane potential, stabilising the myocardium rather than lowering potassium. (Book p975)

items.q: What dose of 10% calcium gluconate does the page give, how fast, and how long does the effect last?
opts: 10 mL intravenously over 2 to 3 minutes, lasting 30 to 60 minutes
10 mL intravenously over 10 minutes, lasting 2 to 6 hours
50 mL infusion over 1 hour, lasting 4 to 6 hours
items.exp: The dose is 10 mL IV over 2 to 3 minutes with an onset of 3 minutes and a duration of 30 to 60 minutes, and 10 mL is stated to contain 90 mg of elemental calcium. (Book p975)

items.q: Fill up: One ampoule of 10% calcium gluconate, 10 mL, contains ______ mg of elemental calcium, and myocardial protection is only temporary because the effect lasts ______ minutes.
items.exp: The bracket gives 90 mg of elemental calcium per 10 mL, and the last bullet records an onset of 3 minutes with cover for only 30 to 60 minutes, which is why a potassium-lowering measure must follow. (Book p975)

items.q: Which insulin regimen appears as the alternative to the 500 mL infusion in the insulin-dextrose entry?
opts: 10 units intravenously stat followed by 50 mL of 50% dextrose
20 units subcutaneously followed by 250 mL of 10% dextrose
10 units intravenously with no dextrose cover
5 units intravenously followed by 500 mL of normal saline
items.exp: The dose line offers 10 U regular insulin in 500 mL of 10% dextrose over 1 hour, or 10 U IV stat followed by 50 mL of 50% dextrose, with 50 mL/hr of 10% dextrose afterwards to prevent hypoglycemia. (Book p975)

items.q: State the onset, peak and duration printed for the insulin-dextrose measure.
opts: Onset 10 to 20 minutes, peak at 30 to 60 minutes, lasting up to 4 to 6 hours
Onset 3 minutes, peak at 30 to 60 minutes, lasting 30 to 60 minutes
Onset 30 minutes, peak at 60 to 90 minutes, lasting 2 to 6 hours
Onset 1 hour, peak at 2 hours, lasting 12 hours
items.exp: Insulin with dextrose is listed with an onset of 10 to 20 minutes, a peak by 30 to 60 minutes and a duration of up to 4 to 6 hours, in contrast with the fast but brief calcium effect. (Book p975)

items.q: Two hours after insulin-dextrose therapy a treated patient becomes sweaty with a capillary glucose of 48 mg/dL. Which part of the printed protocol was intended to prevent exactly this?
opts: The follow-up infusion of 50 mL/hr of 10% dextrose
The initial 10 mL of calcium gluconate
items.exp: A bracket on the dose line carries the instruction to follow with 50 mL/hr of 10% dextrose specifically to prevent hypoglycemia once the insulin is acting. (Book p975)

items.q: What albuterol dose and route does the page give, and what is its onset?
opts: 10 to 20 mg in 4 mL normal saline over 10 minutes by nebulization, onset 30 minutes
2.5 mg in 4 mL saline over 10 minutes by nebulization, onset 5 minutes
10 to 20 mg intravenously over 2 to 3 minutes, onset 30 minutes
items.exp: Albuterol is listed as 10 to 20 mg in 4 mL NS over 10 minutes by nebulization, with onset at 30 minutes, a peak by 60 to 90 minutes and cover for 2 to 6 hours. (Book p975)

items.q: Three of these belong to the acute regimen on this page. Which one does not?
opts: Oral potassium binders as a rapid-acting measure
items.exp: Oral K+ binders are the fourth item but are annotated obsolete, so they are not part of the effective acute trio of calcium, insulin-dextrose and albuterol. (Book p975)

items.q: Assess the two closing lines of the page: I Oral potassium binders are bracketed as obsolete. II Definitive treatment is dialysis whenever chronic kidney disease is present.
items.exp: The binders line reads obsolete in brackets, and the definitive Rx line reads dialysis with the qualifier when CKD is present. (Book p975)

items.q: A dialysis patient misses two sessions and arrives with potassium 8.6 mmol/L, no visible P waves and a QRS of 160 ms. Which row of the ECG table applies, and what is the correct first drug?
opts: The 8 to 9 mmol/L row with atrial standstill, and 10% calcium gluconate 10 mL over 2 to 3 minutes
The above 9 mmol/L sine-wave row, and 10 units of insulin without dextrose
The 6 to 7 mmol/L row of peaked T waves, and nebulized albuterol alone
The 4 mmol/L normal row, and urgent dialysis with no drug first
items.exp: Loss of the P wave with a prolonged QRS at 8 to 9 mmol/L is the atrial standstill row, and the page makes 10% calcium gluconate the drug of choice to stabilise the myocardium before any potassium-lowering step. (Book p975)

items.q: Fill up: Calcium stabilises the myocardium by moving the action-potential threshold to a ______ value while leaving the ______ unchanged, whereas insulin and albuterol both work by ______.
opts: less negative; resting membrane potential; cellular shift of potassium
more negative; resting membrane potential; renal excretion of potassium
less negative; QRS duration; gastrointestinal binding
more positive; action-potential duration; cellular shift of sodium
items.exp: The calcium mechanism is a less negative threshold with an untouched resting potential, and the other two acute measures are both classified as shifting potassium into cells. (Book p975)
